events.invalidation: CORRA_2027-03 back to the 2.775 Dec-26 3m mid or confirmed on-hold with core near 2% and fading oil.
events.rationale: FACT: Global tightening is live (Fed +25bp, BoJ to 1.25%, BoE 6-3 with three hike votes) while US growth gauges and cyclical assets (copper, SPX, tight HY, low VIX) are not in recession. Canada is priced as the exception: CORRA 2.29, 1m path +29bp by year-end, and a 17 Sep sovereign rally. INFERENCE: energy pass-through plus activity 66 make that exception too large; Mar-27 CORRA should move toward the already-higher Jun/Sep 2027 CRA mids as BoC catch-up is pulled forward. That is the pro-growth/cyclical expression: the laggard cyclical central bank, not long AUD after a housing slump or long NZD with labor 32 and no NZ rates. UNKNOWN: whether Saudi supply workaround and core-near-2% CPI let BoC wait through Q1.

events.rationale: FACT: Canada is still running overnight CORRA at 2.29 with headline inflation at 3.0%, while CRAH27 prices only 3.13 and the Fed has already hiked to 3.75-4.00% with SOFR at 3.85. FACT: CA activity is 66 on a Q2 GDP rebound and stronger Ivey PMI; US activity/labor/inflation gauges are 69/75/72. INFERENCE: pessimism about Canadian labor (score 38, employment -42k) is over-discounted as a reason to keep the 2027H1 path capped; a resilient global cycle plus BoC energy-pass-through risk should lift the March 2027 implied rate. UNKNOWN: CFTC/CME positioning and any post-cutoff BoC communication. The pro-growth expression is to pay that still-limited Canada path, not to buy already-high AUD or fade USD.

events.invalidation: CORRA_2027-03 back to the packet Dec-26 3m mid 2.775, or a confirmed Canada demand break with core near 2% and fading energy pass-through.
events.rationale: FACT: CORRA overnight is 2.29 as of 2026-09-17; the 3m strip prices 2.775 by Dec-26, 3.13 by Mar-27 (+84.0bp vs overnight), 3.365 by Jun-27 and a 2028 peak near 3.655. US SOFR jumped to 3.85 after the Fed delivered 25bp to 3.75-4.00%; SR3H7 is 4.565 and SR3U7 peaks at 4.735. Canada Q2 GDP was +0.8% q/q after +0.1% in Q1, Ivey PMI accelerated, household consumption +0.8% q/q and disposable income +2.1% q/q. Headline CPI held at 3.0% y/y with CPI-trim 1.9% and CPI-median 2.0%. BoC minutes flag higher energy pass-through; the last-24 desk thesis says the energy shock is constraining the global easing impulse after the Fed hike, BoJ 25bp to 1.25%, and a BoE 6-3 hold with three hike votes. INFERENCE: 2.29 is an over-insurance setting against the August jobs print, not an equilibrium compatible with still-positive activity and a global tightening regime. Mar-27 at 3.13 still prices a shallow catch-up versus US 4.565 and versus Canada's own 2028 CRA peak near 3.65, so paying Mar-27 owns the residual hike impulse without needing a new 10Y term-premium story. UNKNOWN: whether energy pass-through actually shows up in subsequent CPI, and whether August employment -42k is the start of a demand break.
